principle: The canonical edition supplies meaning, source identity and claim boundaries; it is never the syntactic, rhetorical or titling template for another language. A locale must read as though the story was conceived and narrated in that language.
styleReferencePolicy: External native publications may be used to calibrate register, title instinct, idiom and storytelling rhythm. They are never evidence for story facts; canonical SandhyaKatha sourcing remains authoritative.
